title: Dub 253 Four-bar
notes: FOUR BARS THAT END IN A FILL. 125 BPM, G minor. The kick and the hats are one-bar loops with a PHRASE of four: bars one to three are the plain groove and bar four answers it, the kick with offbeat hits, the hats filling what they left. Underneath, the stab runs a four-bar progression at 1/4 - i, bVII, bVI, v, a chord a bar - and the pad holds the tonic the whole way, so the harmony travels against a groove that returns to the same fourth bar each time round. Start it with the Maschine's PLAY button: the phrase clock is anchored there and nowhere else.

0.why: four on the floor; on bar 4 of every phrase the kick is answered with offbeat hits

3.why: offbeat eighths; the fourth bar of the phrase fills the gaps

4.why: silent in this piece. `empty` is rhythm_reg 0 - no note is written and the pads draw an empty line. Said explicitly rather than by leaving the channel out, because a drum pattern is NOT rewritten on load and an absent block leaves 018's own leftover line playing.

6.why: 1/4 - sixteen quarter notes, a FOUR-bar loop, which is what makes a progression possible at all.

7.why: 1/4 as well - one chord a phrase.

5.why: A1 A1 E1, the same every bar - deliberately, so the chords above are what changes and the ear hears the progression rather than a new bassline.

6.why: A minor, G, F, E - i bVII bVI v, one chord a bar over four bars. The oldest minor progression there is, and it is here because nothing else in the round moves harmonically at all.

7.why: A minor held under the whole four-bar phrase, so the progression moves against a drone rather than in the open.

6.name: Round Bass 1 OB-Xd
6.why: cutoff 0.356, resonance 0.496, sustain 0.308 - heard rather than felt.  Obxd ships this patch at voicecount 0.25, between the scale points for two and three voices, so a triad would lose a note in silence; forced to 1.0 - eight voices - with unison off, because unison stacks voices per NOTE and spends the polyphony a chord needs. Nothing else is overridden: the restore writes saved controllers OVER the preset, so a third value here would be the old patch winning against the new one.

title: Dub 256 Broken Phrygian

The bass runs at 1/8 over TWO bars - root, root, the flat second, root, the flat second - so it repeats twice inside every drum phrase and the fill lands on the second of its two turns.
